thread:
sasha: heads-up — sample-app CI started failing after the latest typegen regen on main. tests broke in integration: positional param call now maps incorrectly.

molly: ugh, saw that. stack trace?

sasha: here's the failing assertion from jest: 

```
 FAIL  integration/createEmbeddings.test.ts
   ✕ embedding request maps wrong (24 ms)
   ● embedding request maps wrong

   expect(received).toEqual(expected) // deep equality

   Received: { input: [ 'foo', 'bar' ] }
   Expected: { input: 'foo' }
```

Looks like our TS client now has an overloaded signature that prefers (options?) instead of single string param. callers that passed just a string are serialized as input: ['string'] instead of 'string'.

jared: that smells like the generator changed the function signature from (text: string, opts?: {}) to (options: {input: string|string[]}) — probably because of the OpenAPI schema's oneOf/anyOf shape. Did regen include the new property ordering?

regen-bot: regen completed for package/sdk-js at 2124999900 — diff: 1 file changed (typegen output).

molly: we need to decide: revert regen, push a compatibility shim in the client (overloaded wrapper), or treat as a minor semver change and publish a new minor release. thoughts?

eve: patch releases should be backwards compatible — this is a breaking change for callers relying on positional string param. semver-wise this is a MAJOR change but our semver policy for generated SDKs treats generator-driven surface changes as potentially minor if we provide backwards-compatible shims.

jared: practically we can add a quick thin wrapper: detect typeof arg1 === 'string' and map to {input: arg1}. That buys time and keeps it a patch. I can open a PR.

sasha: agreed. but we must also update the changelog and add a regen note: "typegen: maintain backward-compatible overload for createEmbeddings". Also add an automated regen-diff check in CI to fail on getters-of-order changes?

molly: we already have a regen-diff job but it only checks file hashes. This was a signature-level change that still passes the hash check in some cases because packaging ordering changed. We should add a lightweight smoke test that calls a few common positional callsites after regen.

jared: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/512 — adds compatibility wrapper + unit tests. CI: https://ci.redwood.dev/10023 — failing on lint because I forgot the typedef. will fix.

ci-bot: build 10023 started, 3 jobs queued.

molly: ok — plan: merge shim as a patch, publish 0.14.1, then follow up with a generator fix so future regens preserve the old overload or keep the shim generator-side. Also add a regen-smoke CI job that runs the sample-app quick integration.

eve: also add a note to the release checklist: "verify positional parameter ergonomics for most-used APIs (embeddings, chat, completions)". we keep hitting this with oneOf/anyOf flattening.

sasha: sounds good. can someone take the changelog bullet? I'll handle the regen-smoke job spec.

jared: i got changelog bullet in the PR description. adding to CHANGELOG.md in the patch branch now.

molly: after the patch publish let's run a full sample-app run on Dedicated env. if green we can roll the patch to the CI image used by sample-app tests.

sasha: one more thing — can we add a small lint rule in typegen that flags moved positional args? maybe compare previous signature AST and warn during regen. low priority but would help.

jared: noted. I'll prototype a signature diff check that runs in ~200ms. filing an issue.

molly: thanks team. follow-up: if anyone sees other unexpected client surface changes post-regen, ping #devex immediately and link the PR.

sasha: thanks :thumbsup:
